Subject: internal: FinServe credit reconciliation (draft)

Markus / Sergio / Grace — I pulled the BrightWave export and the HubSpot contact->lead attribution table. Quick summary of what I’m seeing (numbers pulled from the attached working sheet):

- Total distinct scanned leads (post-dedupe): 87
- Leads that became MQLs within 90 days: 24
- Pipeline attributed to event-sourced MQLs: $312,000
- HubSpot credit allocated to PacificBank (per current tags): 40% of pipeline (~$124,800)
- PacificBank internal claim: ~60% (~$187,200) based on roundtable attendance and perceived influence

Notes on mapping differences:
- We used a multi-touch weighting of 40% first-touch (event scan), 30% owner outreach, 30% product demo follow-up. PacificBank appears to want the roundtable to be weighted as a primary influence for attendees of that session — that would shift ~14 leads into heavier partner credit because several of the converted MQLs attended only the roundtable.
- HubSpot tagging: several BrightWave exported badge emails mapped to existing contacts that had prior product page visits; HubSpot assigned partial credit to ‘organic’ or prior events under our multi-touch rules, lowering the partner percentage.

Proposal (internal):
1) Recompute partner credit for roundtable attendees only (filter = partner_flag == "roundtable") and apply a +20% delta to partner weighting for those leads (i.e., move them from 40% partner to 60%).
2) Provide PacificBank a reconciled CSV (Lead ID, email, original attribution %, revised attribution %, quoted Opp $).
3) Ask finance if a tolerance of +/- 10% on partner credit is acceptable before invoicing adjustments.

I’ve added a small notes column in the workbook explaining each row’s change. If we apply the proposal, PacificBank’s share of attributed pipeline moves to ~55% (~$171k) — still shy of their 60% ask but much closer and defensible.

Flags: this will require a HubSpot manual adjustment (workflows & contact properties) and a short audit trail note on the deal record.

I’ll attach the working workbook after the quick pass.

— Rachel Kim
Marketing Operations
Redwood Inference

Leah / Sam — thanks for the patience while we dug into this. Attached is the reconciled workbook (redwood-sponsorship-recon-20261102.xlsx) and a short summary of changes we propose. TL;DR: we adjusted partner credit for roundtable-only attendees and documented the audit trail. Result: PacificBank credit moves from 40% to 54.8% of the attributed pipeline (new total ~$171,000).

Action items we propose:
- Redwood ops (Rachel) will update HubSpot properties to reflect the revised attribution and add a note on the DEAL-8472 timeline (expected completion tomorrow).
- BrightWave to confirm the exported session list (Sam) — any missed check-ins will change the rows.
- PacificBank to confirm acceptance of the revised credit. If accepted, Redwood will issue a corrected co-marketing invoice reflecting the updated share (finance will confirm final amount).

If you prefer a 15-minute call to walk through the workbook, we can do that tomorrow morning — I can share a short recording of our logic as well (call-recording-20261102.mp3 attached).

Thanks again — we tried to preserve consistent attribution logic while giving reasonable uplift to sponsored roundtable attendees.

Best,
Markus Klein
